newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's NATO bid on right track - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: Romania's NATO bid on right track - U.S. official.

text.p: A senior United States defence official on Thursday praised Romania's bid for early admission into NATO and said the Balkan country was on the right track.
"Romania has taken many excellent steps and is on a very constructive path," Assistant Secretary of Defence Frank Kramer told journalists in Bucharest.
Kramer heads a delegation of U.S. army officers who attend an annual meeting on joint Romanian-U.S. military programmes.
NATO is due to announce at a July summit in Madrid the names of countries that will be invited to negotiate membership in the proposed enlargement.

"But as you know, decisions have yet to be made," Kramer said. "The U.S. has not taken any decisions at all with respect to countries that might be offered membership this July in Madrid. That's true for all the other countries and equally true with respect to Romania," he added.
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are seen as leading contenders, but Romania and Slovenia are also discussed.
"The United States is only one of 16 nations in NATO and NATO works by consensus among the democratic countries and NATO itself likewise has not yet taken any decision."
Kramer said a smooth transition of power during last November's elections as well as a reformist economic programme presented by the new centrist government had a favourable impact in Washington.

"We were extremely encouraged by the elections... by the very courageous programme that you are undertaking economicaly," Kramer said. "All of these are examples of quite positive steps and they are viewed constructively by the U.S."
France, Italy and Spain have already expressed their full support for Romania's bid.
